correctness.rationale: The unit ball is an explicit centrally symmetric octagon. Convexity of the arithmetic endpoint objective reduces its maximum on the product ball to vertex pairs. Dihedral symmetry leaves four vertex classes, whose exact arithmetic values are 1, 2 lambda, max{1/lambda,2 lambda}, and 1/lambda. Hence A_2=max{1/lambda,2 lambda}. The scalar Heinz inequality M_nu(r,s)<=(r+s)/2 gives H_nu<=A_2, while the explicit vertices (1,a) and (-a,1), a=1/lambda-1, give both sum and difference norm equal to max{1/lambda,2 lambda}. Thus equality holds for every nu in [0,1], including all endpoints. The argument covers lambda=1/2 and lambda=1 by the same formulas with degenerate vertices.

value.rationale: The result closes the first and most geometric mixed-exponent endpoint left outside the two displayed branches of a source devoted to exact Heinz constants. It gives the full lambda phase diagram simultaneously for every Heinz parameter nu, identifies a sharp transition at the regular-octagon value lambda=1/sqrt(2), and interpolates canonically between the l_infinity and l_1 endpoints. This is a natural family/invariant gap rather than an arbitrary slice, and the phase transition exposes the competition between the square and diamond facets.
